messages.author: 9072548eb44c9731
messages.subject: syntax for continuous interaction term with inlabru?
parts:
I really like the accessibility of the inlabru package, especially for handling output and plotting predictions. I'd like to run a model with an interaction between two continuous variables but I run into an error when I try to do this in inlabru:

# setting up inla stack
stack1 <- inla.stack(
  tag = "estimation", ## tag
  data = list(julian_lay = dataset$julian_lay), ## response
  A = list(A1, 1), ## projector matrices (SPDE and fixed effects)
  effects = list(
    list(site = seq_len(spde1$n.spde)), ## random field index
    dataset %>%
      as.data.frame() %>%
      transmute(
        Intercept = 1, 
        anom_tmin_mar_may, 
        base_tmin_mar_may
      ) ## fixed effect covariates
  )
)
stack1

# inla model with continuous interaction term
model_spde1 <- inla(
  julian_lay ~ 0 + Intercept + anom_tmin_mar_may*base_tmin_mar_may + f(site, model = spde1),
  family = "gaussian", 
  data = inla.stack.data(stack1),
  control.predictor = list(A = inla.stack.A(stack1)),
  control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE, dic = TRUE, waic = TRUE)
)
summary(model_spde1)

# same using bru() which does not work:
bru_spde1 <- bru(
  julian_lay ~ anom_tmin_mar_may*base_tmin_mar_may + site(map = coordinates, model = spde1),
  family = "gaussian", 
  data = as_Spatial(dataset)
)

And the error looks like this:
Error in `[[<-`(`*tmp*`, ge$f$label, value = smod) : 
  no such index at level 1
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In if (label == "offset") { :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used
2: In if (smod$label == "offset") lbl[[k]] = "offset(offset)" :
  the condition has length > 1 and only the first element will be used

Is there another way to code this with inlabru? I guess I haven't come across an example where this is done so I'm not sure how to set that up.

Thanks,

Jay

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] syntax for continuous interaction term with inlabru?
parts:
Hi,

inlabru separates "model components" from "predictor expressions", and
doesn't support the special "interaction operator *", but instead that
has to be coded explicitly.
For purely additive models, one can use the shortcut of only
specifying model components, which implies that the predictor should
be the sum of the components.

First, add a new column, anom_base =
anom_tmin_mar_may*base_tmin_mar_may to your data object.
Then the "interaction term" is just another ordinary covariate effect,
and the following should work:

bru(
julian_lay ~ anom_tmin_mar_may + base_tmin_mar_may + anom_base +
